blocks.text: 1. **What you agree to.** You let Stackapella use a recording of your singing, made in the app, to make songs' parts in a voice like yours, using AI; to keep a short voice reference made from it for your next songs; and to keep the songs it makes for you to hear.

2. **Your recording.** You record about 30 seconds, singing along with the song, and the app records it live. Record only your own voice. We make a short voice reference from it, and delete the recording itself once your first song is made, or if making it fails.

3. **Your voice reference.** We keep it privately in your account so your next songs need no new recording. Only you can use it, and only for your own songs: we never use it, or your songs, to make a voice for anyone else, or for anything else. We delete it promptly when you delete it in the app or delete your account, and after 12 months in which you make no song with it.

4. **What it sings.** Songs in our library, with their own words, and songs you make in the app, with the words you give them (a hummed tune without words is sung on "oo"). Your words follow our community guidelines: nothing that harasses or deceives, or makes it seem that someone said or sang something they didn't.

5. **Your songs.** They are private to you unless you share one. Everything made this way is marked as AI, in the app and on anything you share, and you won't present it as a real recording of you or anyone else. A song you share can be reported, and we take it down if it breaks these terms or the guidelines. You can delete a song, or every song and your voice reference, at any time in the app.

6. **Your voice in songs you join.** Someone can invite you to sing in a song they made this way. If you agree to that song, a voice like yours sings only the parts given to you, only in that one song. Its owner gets the song with your parts in it, never your recording or your voice reference, and nobody else can use a voice like yours. If you have no saved voice yet, the clip you sing also makes yours, kept for your own songs as in term 3. You see the words before you agree, and a song's words never change once it's made. You can leave the song at any time, and your parts are deleted from it; the owner's own parts play again. We can't recall a copy the owner already downloaded. A song you join counts against its owner's limits, never yours. On a shared page your name shows only if you chose to show it; otherwise the song says a friend sang. Your clip, and the parts made from it, are handled as in term 8.

7. **Limits.** Your first song is free, once per email address. Plus includes 60 minutes of AI singing in each month of your subscription, counted from your renewal day (about 15 songs; every part counts, so four one-minute parts are four minutes); unused minutes don't carry over. Plus given to you free, through a school, a partner or a coach, includes 3 songs in any 30 days. A seat in a choir group covers singing with the group, not songs in your own voice. There is also a daily limit for everyone. Hearing a song you've already made, and sharing it, are always free; downloading a song needs Plus.

8. **Your data.** Your songs are made on the servers of our GPU provider, Modal, in the United States: your clip, the voice made from it and the parts made in it are kept encrypted there for up to 7 days, then deleted; the same for a clip you sing to join someone's song. We keep your voice reference, your songs, how many you've made, and which version of these terms you accepted and when; your data download says when your reference was saved and last used. We never use them to identify you. To keep the free song to one per person, once you've made it we keep a one-way code made from your email address (and any Apple or Google account you sign in with), even after you delete your account; it can't be turned back into your address, and it's used for nothing else.
9. **Your promise.** The recording is your own singing, and you're 18 or over.
10. **Changes.** If we change these terms, we'll ask you to accept them again before your next song.
